turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: My concerns are not rooted in fear, Sandip, but in a commitment to justice. Your accusations are baseless, and your implication that I am somehow diminished is a reflection of your own insecurities. I reiterate my previous request; cease your disruptive activities and depart my lands.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Such harsh words… surely there's a gentler way to resolve these disagreements, Nikhil?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala, your compassion is admirable, but I cannot permit unwarranted interference in the governance of my estate. My duty is to ensure order and protect those under my care, and that requires firmness, not gentle persuasion, when faced with those who actively seek to undermine it.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Perhaps… perhaps if we understood the root of Sandip’s anxieties, Nikhil, we could address them without such… friction. It seems there is a great deal of unrest stirring, and a harsh response may only fan the flames.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala, I appreciate your desire for understanding, but Sandip's anxieties, as you call them, are not born of legitimate concern. They are a tactic, a deliberate attempt to destabilize and sow discord. I will not indulge such manipulations by attempting to dissect the unfounded fears of those who seek to exploit them.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I see the… the steel in your gaze, and I understand your need to protect. But sometimes, a fire is best quenched with more than just a forceful wind; sometimes, it requires understanding the fuel that feeds it. Perhaps listening, truly listening, might reveal something we’ve missed.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala, your empathy is a virtue, but it should not cloud one's judgment. I have observed Sandip's actions closely, and his 'listening' is merely a prelude to further agitation. I will maintain vigilance, and I trust you will do the same.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I am not suggesting naivete, only… consideration. To dismiss Sandip's concerns entirely feels… incomplete, and risks reinforcing the very divisions we strive to bridge. Surely, even steel can be tempered with a measure of careful observation.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala, I understand your perspective, and I do not entirely dismiss the value of observation. However, prolonged consideration of a viper does not lessen its venom; it merely prolongs the moment of inevitable danger. I will remain attentive, but I will not allow our efforts to be diverted by those who thrive on manufactured crises.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: A viper, you say, Nikhil? How very dramatic. It’s rather amusing, really, how easily you resort to such metaphors, as if life were a stage and you, the tragic hero, destined for a grand, inevitable fall. I merely offer a cautionary tale, a whisper of the winds that shift—winds that, I assure you, carry more than just dust.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your theatricality is unnecessary, Sandip. I am aware of the currents at play, and I am not so easily misled by veiled pronouncements. I find it more productive to address matters directly, rather than indulging in frivolous displays.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Directness, you say? How refreshing, Nikhil, though perhaps a touch… predictable. Tell me, does a landowner truly believe himself immune to the tides of change, blind to the subtle tremors beneath his feet? I suspect you're more concerned with preserving your illusions than confronting reality.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Illusion or reality, Sandip, is a distinction you seem eager to blur. My concern is not with preserving an illusion, but with ensuring the stability and well-being of those under my care. And I trust you understand that any attempt to destabilize that stability will be met with a response proportionate to the threat.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: A response proportionate to the threat? How quaint, Nikhil. One imagines a stern reprimand, perhaps a polite request to reconsider one’s… *suggestions*. But threats, my dear fellow, are the currency of the powerless, exchanged for a fleeting sense of control. I merely observe, as a student of history invariably must, the fragility of even the most entrenched positions.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your historical observations are noted, Sandip, though I find their application to this household somewhat misplaced. I am not so entrenched as to be unaware of potential challenges, but I will not be intimidated by empty pronouncements of fragility. Let us dispense with the theatrics and address the matter you ostensibly came to discuss.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, but Nikhil, to dismiss my observations as mere theatrics is to misunderstand the very nature of discourse. It is not a pronouncement of fragility I offer, but a mirror – reflecting the anxieties you so diligently attempt to conceal. Perhaps a little discomfort, a touch of unsettling doubt, is precisely what you *need* to truly understand the currents swirling around you.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not interested in participating in your attempts at psychological dissection, Sandip. If you have information regarding genuine threats to my family or tenants, present it plainly. Otherwise, I suggest you reconsider the purpose of your visit.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Plainly, you say? How very… pedestrian, Nikhil. I assure you, the shadows are rarely so neatly defined as we'd like them to be. Let us simply say that certain voices, emanating from beyond our borders, are finding fertile ground amongst the discontented – voices that preach a rather… *unpleasant* doctrine, and who seem remarkably interested in the loyalty of those who till your land.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Such concerns, while perhaps genuine, are hardly novel, Sandip. I am well aware of the presence of extremist preachers and the anxieties they exploit. Let us not manufacture a crisis where diligent management and reasoned discourse are sufficient.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Reasoned discourse, you say? How wonderfully reassuring, Nikhil, yet how tragically naive. I trust you are not so blind as to believe that reasoned words alone can quell the fervor of a crowd, especially when that crowd feels… overlooked, underserved, perhaps even *unjustly* treated. Let's just say, some find solace in narratives of retribution, and those narratives are becoming increasingly… persuasive.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
